radiology_report:
Subject: mpMRI Prostate | Facility: Catharina Ziekenhuis, Eindhoven | Date: 15 January 2025

Clinical Indication: Assessment of elevated PSA (19.0) alongside a previously positive biopsy.

FINDINGS: The gland spans 65.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a discrete, intensely hypointense focus within the right posterior peripheral zone at mid-gland, occupying roughly 12 × 8 × 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging confirms restricted diffusion, mirrored by low ADC signal. Post-contrast phases show early, focal enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Seminal vesicles remain clear. No extraprostatic spread or suspicious nodal enlargement is detected. Bladder and rectal walls appear intact.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 4 lesion located in the right mid peripheral zone. Prostate volume 65.0 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.29 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.7148355.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient was seen in June 2024 after PSA climbed to 14.6 ng/mL in November 2023. Digital rectal examination revealed a small right-sided nodule. Catharina Ziekenhuis conducted a multiparametric MRI that yielded a PI-RADS 4 result. With the earlier biopsy confirming Gleason 4+3 disease alongside these new imaging markers, a referral to the urology outpatient clinic was processed for further clinical assessment.
